<!--
Shared quarto-live boot include for the in-browser climt demo pages.

Include it once, near the top of any `format: live-html` / `engine: jupyter`
page, with a Quarto include shortcode pointing at this file (see
radiative-transfer/09-live-rce.qmd for the exact line). Do NOT repeat the
literal include shortcode in this comment: Quarto resolves include shortcodes
at the text level, before HTML comments are stripped, so a literal one here
would make this file include itself.

It boots Pyodide, micropip-installs the pinned pure-Python climt wheel (the
GitHub release asset — the wheel URL/tag is defined ONCE here), and defines
`integrate_to_equilibrium(...)` for the RCE pages.

The `integrate_to_equilibrium` body below is duplicated in the natively
testable twin `docs/radiative-transfer/_live/rce_helpers.py`; keep the two
bodies IDENTICAL (only `tests/test_live_rce_demo.py` guards the twin).
-->

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: true
#| edit: false
# The climt wheel is installed by micropip at document setup (before any cell
# runs) via the `pyodide: packages:` block in the page front matter — see
# radiative-transfer/09-live-rce.qmd. Installing here with `await
# micropip.install(...)` instead would race: quarto-live does not await one
# autorun cell's async work before starting the next, so a downstream cell can
# run before the wheel finishes installing. So this cell is synchronous.
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import climt
from sympl import AdamsBashforth
from datetime import timedelta


def integrate_to_equilibrium(tendency_components, stepper_components, state,
                             timestep, n_steps):
    """Step tendency + stepper components forward toward radiative equilibrium.

    Keep this body in sync with the copy in
    docs/radiative-transfer/_live/rce_helpers.py.

    Update order matters: the new (prognostic) state is applied *before* the
    diagnostics, so flux diagnostics (e.g. the longwave fluxes SlabSurface
    consumes) survive into the next step instead of being clobbered by the
    stepper carrying those fields forward at their pre-step value.
    """
    model = AdamsBashforth(list(tendency_components))
    for _ in range(n_steps):
        diagnostics, new_state = model(state, timestep)
        state.update(new_state)
        state.update(diagnostics)
        for stepper in stepper_components:
            s_diag, s_new = stepper(state, timestep)
            state.update(s_new)
            state.update(s_diag)
        state["time"] += timestep
    return state


# End on a plain statement (not a def): quarto-live captures each cell's final
# value for display, and marshalling a bare function object through JS interop
# yields an unhashable JsProxy that aborts the cell.
print("climt", climt.__version__, "ready — has_fortran:", climt.has_fortran_extensions())
```
